title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus
note: arXiv:2609.03344, v1, 12 pages, 3 figures, physics.soc-ph. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, no journal version. Source for equations (1)-(20), thresholds 0.50/0.40/~0.420, Table 1, and all verbatim quotations in the body.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
note: Field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school students. 48%/127% improvement, 17% decline after access removed, term "crutch" in abstract.

title: Think First, ChatGPT Later: Guiding Human–AI Collaboration for Learning Gains in Independent Human Creativity
note: N=196 university students, three groups, reversal on second (independent) task.

title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
container-title: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
note: 319 knowledge workers, 936 real-world task examples. Reports a negative relationship between trust in AI and enactment of critical thinking.

title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
note: Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Project site: brainonllm.com. Two figures widely circulated in press coverage could not be confirmed in the abstract or project site and were excluded from the body.

title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
Experimental evidence for tipping points in social convention
note: Cited by the paper as precedent for tipping points in social convention.

title: Allee Effects in Ecology and Conservation

title: Cognitive offloading
note: Definition of cognitive offloading, used by the paper. Also bundled under this reference number: D. C. title: AI Index 2026
note: 2025 data. Global adoption 53%, United States 28.3%, organizations 88%. Contrasting US figure of 54% is the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's own tracker for August 2025.

title: OECD, Eurostat and Pew Research Center individual AI-adoption surveys
note: OECD member-country surveys (2025 data), average 36.8%. Eurostat ages 16-74, 32.7% (2025, first year with a generative AI question). Pew Research Center survey of US adults, 44% for ChatGPT alone / 49% for chatbots overall (February 2026, n=5,119). None of the three source pages could be opened directly; all rest on search summaries.

title: Digital Education Outlook 2026
note: Source for the statement that advantage disappears or reverses when AI access is removed. Its evidence plausibly overlaps with reference 2 (Bastani et al.), so the body does not describe it as independent confirmation.

title: 2025 Survey on Internet Usage (2025 인터넷이용실태조사)
note: 50,750 household members surveyed. Generative AI experience rate 44.5%, up 11.2 percentage points year on year.

title: Diary study of enforced disconnection from AI assistants
note: 10 participants, 4 days. Qualitative study of imposed disconnection rather than voluntary abandonment.

title: 2026 CHI-family study on the gap between self-reported AI use and perceived peer use
note: Reports a 30-percentage-point gap, interpreted as social desirability bias. Reached via search summary; original bibliographic record could not be confirmed.

title: NBER working papers on school smartphone-ban policy effects
note: Two strands: one reporting a significant test-score increase in a large school district, and a 2026 national analysis reporting a near-zero effect for the locked-pouch approach. Both are stated in the body.

title: "AI-free day" recommendation from consulting industry sources
note: Original report title and publication date could not be confirmed at a primary source, so the body does not attribute it to a named firm. Corporate AI-metric tracking figures likewise come via consulting-industry aggregation.
